title: Linux containment step 1: report containment from a probe, not a PATH lookup

AC4.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08 after the AC13 amendment cleared all confirmations. Ran probe.test.ts fresh: 29 pass / 0 fail, 111 expect() calls. Failure path returns the launcher's stderr in detail with only the trailing newline trimmed (asserted with toBe against the literal 'bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied'); success returns exactly {layer,ok} — asserted with toEqual, so an added detail would fail. Spawn is injected in every case; the file launches no launcher.

AC5.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08 in the same probe.test.ts run (29 pass). Three probeContainment calls produce one fake-spawn invocation and return the identical object; the cache holds even when a later caller passes different platform/spawn options, so it is a bound on spawns rather than a per-argument memo. Falsifiable counterpart asserts runContainmentProbe spawns on every call (2 calls, 2 spawns), so the count above cannot be one because the fake is unreachable.

AC6.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08. sandbox.test.ts ran clean within a 60 pass / 0 fail batch. Nothing reads available unless a probe confirmed it AND the trial exercised it; a clean darwin trial leaves allowlist/masking as 'unprobed' rather than confirmed. The Linux unavailable reason names the kernel release and the withheld facility and asserts not.toContain('linux'); a different injected release changes the sentence, so it is a fact about the host and not a constant. Also re-checked live on this host in both states via the probe's seam: working prints 'Containment probe: OK', shimmed prints FAILED with the kernel-named reason.

AC7.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08. capability-matrix.doc-sync.test.ts ran clean in the 60 pass batch. It iterates the exported CAPABILITY_STATUSES rather than a hand-written list, so all three values are covered and a fourth added to the type fails rather than being skipped. Falsifiability was itself repaired earlier in this flow after a reviewer's mutation showed the original 'falsifiable' cases were tautologies: the current one doctors the parsed section and asserts the same filter now reports 'unavailable' missing, plus checks the parse is non-empty and that a heading rename throws.

AC8.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08 by running the fail-closed tests rather than only diffing: adapter.restricted-fail-closed.test.ts, wrap.test.ts and detect.test.ts together are 26 pass / 0 fail, and all three files are absent from the branch diff — unmodified, as the criterion requires. adapter.ts, wrap.ts, bwrap.ts, seatbelt.ts and profile.ts are also absent from the diff. detect.ts IS modified (+20/-5: a corrected header comment, an exported BWRAP_INSTALL_HINT, and its reason string using it) but its own test passes unmodified, so behaviour is unchanged. Escape hatches live in harness.ts and shell-exec-tool.ts, neither touched.

AC12.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08: install-global.test.ts 12 pass / 0 fail, 125 expect() calls. install.sh runs 'keryx sandbox status' from the keryx it just installed — no 'command -v bwrap' remains in the file. The broken-shim case emits the uid-map error and the installer prints 'Containment probe: FAILED', quotes the launcher verbatim, names the AppArmor profile, and never says containment is available; the working shim (which execs past the --) yields 'Containment probe: OK' and exactly two 'confirmed by a trial' rows. Also covered: absent launcher, the fail-safe branch, project-install delegation, three hostile TMPDIRs and a noisy failing keryx asserted on bytes.

AC13.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08 against the amended wording, and now confirmable IN FULL — checked rather than assumed. Empirical output check: 136 lines of real rendered output captured across five live invocations (containment working and containment broken via the probe's seam, each plain and --json, plus --help) contain neither 'apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns' nor even the word 'sysctl'. The failing state names the AppArmor profile: 'Remediation: grant the user namespace to /usr/bin/bwrap alone with an AppArmor profile at /etc/apparmor.d/bwrap...'. Enforced by test, not inspection: four not.toContain assertions in probe.test.ts, sandbox.test.ts, capability-matrix.doc-sync.test.ts and install-global.test.ts, all green. Source audit: exactly 7 occurrences under src/ and scripts/ — 4 are those assertions, 3 are comments explaining ADR-0010's rejection (probe.test.ts, sandbox.test.ts, probe.ts). Zero are rendering paths or output strings. Every occurrence falls inside the amendment's explicit allowance.

AC14.note: Re-verified 2026-08-08. purity.test.ts ran clean in the 60 pass batch: the pure modules cannot spawn directly (import-statement matching, not substring, so a doc comment can neither trip nor satisfy it) nor transitively (fixed-point closure over relative imports, which covers the barrel route index.ts opened). Direct-spawner set pinned to probe.ts + tls-ca.ts; probe.ts confirmed to import node:child_process and to expose 'spawn?: ProbeSpawn'. package.json and bun.lock are absent from the branch diff, so no new dependency; wrap.ts, bwrap.ts, seatbelt.ts, profile.ts and adapter.ts are absent too, as the criterion names.

AC4: probe.test.ts: 29 tests over an injected spawn. Failure reports the launcher stderr verbatim (bwrap: setting up uid map: Permission denied, only the trailing newline trimmed); success returns {layer,ok} with no detail, cause or remediation. Control characters stripped and output capped, asserted on bytes.

AC5: probeContainment caches process-globally: 3 calls, 1 spawn; cache holds across differing options. Falsifiable counterpart proves runContainmentProbe spawns every time. Wiring proven separately in sandbox.test.ts by priming the cache and asserting buildSandboxReport reuses it (spawns stays 1) — the composition a cacheProbe boolean had made untestable.

AC6: sandbox.test.ts: 29 tests, platform/launcher/probe/kernel injected. No row reads available unless the probe confirmed it AND the trial exercised it (coveredByProbe -> the unprobed finding). Linux unavailable reason names the kernel release and the withheld facility, never the string linux, and only when the probe identified a userns cause. Live-verified both ways on Ubuntu 24.04 kernel 6.8.0-136-generic via the injectable seam.

AC7: capability-matrix.doc-sync.test.ts: 13 tests iterating CAPABILITY_STATUSES, so a fourth state cannot be added and left undocumented. Falsifiability was fixed after a reviewer mutation proved the original 'falsifiable' cases were tautologies: the replacement doctors the parsed section and asserts the same filter now reports the state missing. A separate runbook-sync test in sandbox.test.ts covers the fifth user-visible finding (unprobed), which the matrix-only test could not see.

AC8: adapter.ts, wrap.ts, bwrap.ts, seatbelt.ts and profile.ts are absent from the full branch diff (git diff --name-only, empty). Escape hatches untouched: KERYX_DANGEROUSLY_DISABLE_SANDBOX and KERYX_SANDBOX_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED live in harness.ts and shell-exec-tool.ts, neither in the diff. Fail-closed tests unmodified and green. Verified independently in review rounds 2-6.

AC12: install.sh delegates to the keryx it just installed. install-global.test.ts: 12 pass. Shims cover absent bwrap, a bwrap that fails with the uid-map error (verbatim quote + AppArmor remediation, no sysctl), and one that contains. Plus the fail-safe branch (a keryx that cannot start claims nothing, either way, and still exits 0), the project-install delegation shape, three hostile TMPDIRs, and a noisy failing keryx asserted on bytes. Both bash tests falsified by hand.

AC13: PARTIAL, deliberately, and recorded rather than silently confirmed. R8's substance holds: no rendering path, output string or test fixture names the sysctl as a remedy, enforced by four not.toContain assertions (probe.test.ts, sandbox.test.ts, capability-matrix.doc-sync.test.ts, install-global.test.ts). All 15 repo mentions are rejections, statements of the kernel default, or negative assertions. The frozen wording also forbids COMMENTS from naming it; three comments introduced here do, each while explaining why ADR-0010 rejected it. Flagged by review rounds 4-6; the AC's letter is unmet, its intent is met and enforced.

AC14: No new npm dependency (package.json absent from the diff). purity.test.ts enforces N3 by test rather than by diff inspection: the pure modules cannot spawn directly or transitively (fixed-point closure over relative imports, so the barrel route is covered), matching import statements rather than substrings so a doc comment cannot trip it and cannot satisfy it. probe.ts performs no spawn when its seam is injected. Writing the guard found a real fact: tls-ca.ts also spawns, so the spawning set is computed from source rather than hand-maintained.
draft PR: https://github.com/MrCipherSmith/keryx/pull/259

AC13 as frozen is unsatisfiable: it forbids any comment or test fixture from naming kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns while also requiring enforcement 'by a test, not by inspection' -- and such a test must contain the literal string to assert its absence. It also over-reaches the requirement it implements: specification R8 constrains OUTPUT (what a user is shown), not source comments. The three comments that name the sysctl sit beside the assertions that ban it and state why ADR-0010 rejected it; removing the name would leave the ban unexplained and invite its reintroduction. Narrowing AC13 to rendering paths and output strings, and explicitly permitting the name in tests and comments that enforce or explain the ban. Intent is unchanged: the sysctl is never offered to a user as a remedy. Authorised by the repository owner, 2026-08-08.
Re-freeze after editing the AC13 text itself; the previous ac update recorded the rationale but snapshotted the pre-edit wording.
